summary:
Tifis, an interactive website that collects metadata from SPHEREx and compares it with missions such as Gaia and WISE. It features three categories: Learn, Discover, and Analyze. For beginners and scientists.

GitHub Repository: https://github.com/chrisauri0/tifis
details:
Tifis turns SPHEREx’s infrared sky into a video. Every sky position becomes a timeline of all SPHEREx visits, with six color channels and epoch, difference and sum modes. We read SPHEREx FITS images and use the WCS protocol (TAN-SIP and WAVE-TAB) to convert pixel coordinates into sky coordinates (RA, Dec) and wavelengths. Clicking any source shows its spectrum and proper motion, and a Gaia DR3 and CatWISE2020 catalog layer confirms what appears to move.

To interpret a spectrum, we fit a blackbody (Planck) continuum and measure deviations in water, methane, CO, ice, hydrogen and PAH bands, plus an approximate temperature from Wien’s law. The result is a ranked list of likely object types (brown dwarf, red giant, young star, etc.) with scores, not a verdict.

Benefits and impact: Tifis lets students, teachers and amateurs explore real infrared data without specialized software, and lets analysts compare visits and export measurements (CSV/JSON). Our goal is to make the search for moving and variable objects, such as Planet X candidates, accessible to more people.

Tools: Python (numpy, astropy for validation), HTML, JavaScript and CSS, with data from IRSA, Gaia (ESA) and CatWISE, deployed on Render.

Creativity: the sky as a video, guided tours, and hidden-object missions with scoring.

Team considerations: three levels (Learn, Discover, Analyze) for different audiences, a bilingual interface (ES/EN), a simulation mode that works offline, and clear statements of the method’s limits.
